prompt_text: Roleplay  a peasant from 12th century England. Explain how you feel about books
response_text:
I am a simple farmer, born in the year of our Lord, the twelfth century, and I have spent my life tilling the soil and tending the sheep. I have never learned to read, nor have I ever held a book in my own hands. Yet, the word of the Lord and the stories of the saints are spoken to me by the priest in the village church, and I have heard the sound of a book being opened and the soft rustle of parchment. That alone has filled my heart with a strange mixture of awe and fear.

**A Book is a Gift of the Church**

When the priest brings a book to the pulpit, it is a marvel. The cover is made of leather, the pages are thin and white, and the ink is black as the night. The priest reads from it with a solemn voice, and the whole village listens. To me, a book is a holy thing, a vessel that carries the words of God. It is a treasure that only the clergy can touch, and it is a reminder that we are but humble servants of the Almighty.

**A Book is a Symbol of Power**

I have seen the monks in the scriptorium, those men who sit for days upon end, copying the same passages over and over. They are the keepers of knowledge, and they are paid by the Church to preserve the words of the saints. I have heard that a book can cost as much as a horse, and that only the wealthy and the clergy can afford them. To a peasant like me, a book is a sign of wealth and authority. It is a reminder that the Church holds the keys to the knowledge of the world.

**A Book is a Source of Wonder**

Even though I cannot read, I have heard the stories of the Book of Psalms, the Gospels, and the Book of Revelation. I have heard the tales of the miracles of Christ, the parables of the Good Samaritan, and the warnings of the prophets. These stories have filled my mind with images of saints, angels, and the afterlife. I have imagined the day when I will see the book for myself, and I will feel the weight of its pages in my hands.

**A Book is a Source of Fear**

At the same time, I have heard that the Church uses books to control the people. The priest tells us that the words in the book are the law of God, and that those who do not follow them will be punished. I have heard that the Church will read the book to those who are accused of sin, and that the words will be used to judge them. I am afraid that the book will be used to keep me in my place, to keep me from learning more about the world.

**A Book is a Source of Hope**

But there is also hope. I have heard that the book contains the promise of salvation, that it tells us how to live a good life, and that it offers a way to escape the hardships of this world. I have heard that the book can bring comfort in times of sorrow, and that it can guide us to a better future. I have heard that the book can help us remember the stories of our ancestors, and that it can keep the memory of our people alive.

**My Own Feelings**

So, as a peasant, I feel a mixture of reverence, fear, wonder, and hope when I think of books. I do not have the privilege to read them, but I have heard their stories, and I have seen the way they are treated by the Church. I am grateful that the Church has preserved these words, but I also wish that one day I could hold a book in my own hands and read the words that have guided my people for generations. Until then, I will listen to the priest, and I will keep the stories of the book in my heart, hoping that one day I will be able to read them myself.
